mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in a month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in a single month
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a pre-tightening baseline (p > 0.1), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 4% in any month during the period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 6.5% for two consecutive months is associated with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as higher labor market disengagement reduces consumer wealth and corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: Over 12 months, the 60-day forward return is not negative in more than 40% of UNRATE-up periods (binomial test p > 0.3).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in HOUST (industrial production) exceeding the prior month's level by at least 2% coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as strong supply-side momentum boosts investor confidence and equity valuation.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly growth > +2% vs prior month
failure_condition: Across 10 such events, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 3% over two months signals supply-side weakness, which predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return via reduced corporate earnings growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -3% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 5 such supply contraction episodes, the 20-day forward return is not negative (mean p > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for three consecutive months in a non-recessionary regime, it predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as lower policy rates incentivize equity investment.
failure_condition: Over 12 such 3-month periods, the 60-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PAYEMS (employment months) below 130,000 for a month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market weakness erodes consumer spending and corporate profit expectations.
failure_condition: In 8 such episodes, the 20-day forward return is not negative (mean p > 0.25).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in GDPC1 (GDP chained) growth exceeding 4% above the prior month's rate is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as strong demand supports equity valuation expansion.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly growth > +4% vs prior month
failure_condition: Across 7 such acceleration events, the 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.18).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE for two consecutive months indicate dual headwinds that jointly depress investor sentiment and corporate earnings prospects, producing a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < prev AND UNRATE < prev for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 10 such interaction events, the 20-day forward return is not negative in more than 50% (binomial p < 0.5).
